articles.title: Well how correct do we need it to be?
Fragments: November 20
articles.summary: Marcus Borg recounts an experiment to investigate if healthy code was cheaper for agents to review. Between a typical unhealthy pull request (CodeHealth 2.8) and a typical healthy one (9.7), that adds...
articles.description: Marcus Borg recounts an experiment to investigate if healthy code was cheaper for agents to review. Between a typical unhealthy pull request (CodeHealth 2.8) and a typical healthy one (9.7), that adds up to 22 to 35%. The measures of health come from CodeScene. The experiment looked at three LLMs, 465 pull requests on 246 open source repositories.
